notes: All six DOIs resolved on the Crossref works API; abstracts cross-checked on Europe PMC (MED records for five papers, PPR19818 for the bioRxiv preprint).

Methods read on the bioRxiv full-text page (Shimoura) and on PMC full texts: PMC9167055 (EDEN), PMC12597029 (Plesser), PMC6230720 (Blundell), PMC11405706 (NIR), PMC9272742 (NEURON). nature.com redirected to a login page, so NIR was read on PMC.
Crossref says the Shimoura preprint is-preprint-of Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1244116. The Zenodo API returned HTTP 504 on three attempts, so that record's title, venue and code URL are unverified.
Crossref renders the Plesser title separator as a replacement character; the citation uses Europe PMC's rendering (hyphen). The exact punctuation is unverified.
Method-level details come from tool summaries of the full-text pages. Paraphrased only; no result claims are made for NeuroSem.

rows.citation: Shimoura RO, Kamiji NL, de Oliveira Pena RF, et al. (2018). Reimplementation of the Potjans-Diesmann cortical microcircuit model: from NEST to Brian. bioRxiv (preprint).
rows.model_type: spiking point-neuron (LIF) cortical microcircuit network; NEST to Brian 2 manual reimplementation
rows.controlled_mutations: no; no deliberate fault seeding, though using an approximate equation instead of the exact one was reported to shift some population rates
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; compares several network input regimes (Poisson background, DC input, layer-independent input, parameter variations), not single-cell current-clamp protocols
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; population firing-rate and ISI coefficient-of-variation distributions compared with Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests, no single-cell eFEL features
rows.protocol_optimization: no; input conditions were chosen to mirror the original article, with no selection or minimisation
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; one model, one translation, no discovery/held-out split
rows.software: Brian 2 reimplementation code: unverified (the Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.1244116 named by Crossref returned HTTP 504)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: One manual cross-simulator translation checked by network statistics. NeuroSem would test many single-cell NeuroML edits with calibrated per-feature tolerances, seeded single-fault mutants, and optimised current-clamp batteries evaluated on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, 7 authors, posted 2018-01-16, preprint-of relation); Europe PMC PPR19818 abstract; bioRxiv full-text page for the comparison method and the approximate-equation discrepancy
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:biorxiv.org (same neuron model different simulators discrepancies NEURON Brian NEST translation equivalence single cell)

rows.citation: Plesser HE, Davison AP, Diesmann M, et al. (2025). Building on models-a perspective for computational neuroscience. Cerebral Cortex, 35, bhaf295.
rows.model_type: spiking cortical microcircuit network (Potjans-Diesmann) used as a cross-simulator benchmark; perspective/workshop report
rows.controlled_mutations: no; a perspective report with no fault seeding
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; discusses reproducing the model's standard activity statistics, not stimulus batteries
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; describes statistical-level comparison using firing-rate distributions, ISI CV and correlations, since exact numerical matching across simulators is infeasible
rows.software: none (discusses NEST, GPU and neuromorphic simulators, the NeuroML 2 version, and OSB Model Validation (OMV) for per-change regression runs; no tool released)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Context only: it motivates statistical correctness benchmarks and OMV-style regression, but for one network benchmark. NeuroSem targets single-cell NeuroML edits with mutation-calibrated, optimised current-clamp batteries and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (16 authors, vol 35, article bhaf295, online 2025-11-09); Europe PMC MED 41206945 abstract; PMC12597029 full text for the benchmark-statistics and OMV discussion

rows.model_type: general-purpose biophysical neuron simulator engineering (NEURON/CoreNEURON, NMODL source-to-source compiler)

rows.citation: Panagiotou S, Sidiropoulos H, Soudris D, et al. (2022). EDEN: A High-Performance, General-Purpose, NeuroML-Based Neural Simulator. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics, 16, 724336.
rows.model_type: NeuroML v2 simulator; correctness checked on NeuroML-DB single-cell models (conductance-based, incl. multicompartment) and three published networks
rows.controlled_mutations: no; compares a new simulator against NEURON without seeded faults
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; single-cell checks use one fixed somatic DC current-clamp step for every model
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; ISI percent difference and a NeuroML-DB waveform similarity metric for cells; network rate, ISI and correlation statistics with effect sizes
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; no discovery/held-out split, though the cell check spans a large NeuroML-DB model set
rows.software: EDEN https://gitlab.com/neurocomputing-lab/Inferior_OliveEMC/eden (GitLab page shows GPL-3.0-or-later); PyPI eden-simulator 0.2.3 https://pypi.org/project/eden-simulator/
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: A large-scale, canonical single-protocol cross-simulator check for NeuroML cells, close to NeuroSem's baseline. NeuroSem would add mutation-calibrated tolerances, multi-protocol fingerprints, greedy battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (5 authors, vol 16, article 724336, 2022-05-20); Europe PMC MED 35669596 abstract; PMC9167055 full text for verification protocol and metrics; PyPI JSON API; GitLab project page for license

rows.citation: Pedersen JE, Abreu S, Jobst M, et al. (2024). Neuromorphic intermediate representation: A unified instruction set for interoperable brain-inspired computing. Nature Communications, 15, 8122.
rows.model_type: spiking neural network intermediate representation (LIF neuron, spiking CNN, spiking RNN) across neuromorphic simulators and hardware
rows.controlled_mutations: no; no fault seeding, only natural cross-platform differences
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; a single LIF neuron input plus dataset inputs for two networks, not designed stimulation protocols
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; membrane-trace and spike alignment, spike counts, hidden-layer rate cosine similarity and task accuracy, not eFEL-style features
rows.software: NIR https://github.com/neuromorphs/NIR (GitHub API license: BSD-3-Clause); PyPI nir 1.0.8
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Adjacent problem of preserving behaviour under translation, for SNNs on neuromorphic platforms. It attributes divergences to discretisation, quantisation and non-determinism, but without a testing method. NeuroSem would focus on conductance-based NeuroML with mutation-calibrated protocol batteries.
